title: What do we need to measure to find the area of a crosspath?
description: A plot fourteen metres by twelve metres has a crosspath made of two paths that cross. The two path widths are the extra measurements needed, and the small crossing rectangle is counted only once. The result is written as a formula and checked with chosen widths.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the areas of the two paths and take away the crossing rectangle that was counted twice. Watch for children who add the two path areas and forget the crossing.

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 3)
video_script.why: The child finds the area of a crosspath by adding the areas of two rectangles and taking away the part counted twice, and writes a formula from chosen widths.
video_script.substitution: Add the areas of the two paths, take away the crossing rectangle once, and check by splitting the crosspath with no overlap.
video_script.anchor: the plot of the book, fourteen metres by twelve metres, with a crosspath
video_script.payoff_line: the area of the crosspath is thirty six square metres

final_answer.value: Area = 14p + 12q − pq, which is 36 m² when the widths are 1 m and 2 m

hold_back: the area of the crosspath is 36 m²
never_show: the area of the crosspath, before the answer beat
maths_rules: plot 14 m by 12 m; the path along the 14 m side has width p, the path along the 12 m side has width q
path areas: 14 × p and 12 × q; the crossing rectangle p × q is counted twice
video_script.design: One idea: add the two paths and take away the crossing counted twice. The plot with its crosspath stays on stage; the widths are chosen, as the book asks.
open_questions: The book figure is not in the extracted text; the picture is drawn from the question, with one path running along each side of the plot and crossing once.
